## Database Content Overview

```{r}
#| label: database-statistics
#| include: false

data_database_statistics <-
  load_database_statistics(
    path_database = path_to_vegvault,
    list_build_manifest = list_build_manifest
  )

label_count <-
  scales::label_comma()

label_size <-
  scales::label_bytes(units = "auto_binary", accuracy = 0.1)
```

[VegVault]{.vegvault} `r db_version` is a comprehensive [SQLite database]{.database} (`r label_size(dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, size_bytes))`) that integrates global vegetation data spanning both [contemporary]{.neo-vegetation} and [paleovegetation]{.paleo} records.
This unified database combines [fossil pollen]{.paleo} records, [contemporary vegetation plots]{.neo-vegetation}, [functional trait]{.traits} measurements, and associated [abiotic environmental data]{.abiotic} to provide an unprecedented resource for vegetation ecology research.

The database consists of `r dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, n_tables)` interconnected tables with `r dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, n_columns)` fields (variables).
For detailed technical information, see our [Database Structure](database_structure.qmd) documentation.
What changed between versions is on the [changelog page](database_changelog.qmd).

## Database Statistics

**VegVault `r db_version` contains:**

|||
|-----|-----|
| **Datasets** | `r label_count(dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, n_datasets))` |
| **Samples** | `r label_count(dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, n_samples))` |
| **Taxa** | `r label_count(dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, n_taxa))` |
| **Trait Domains** | `r dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, n_trait_domains)` |
| **Trait Values** | `r label_count(dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, n_trait_values))` |
| **Abiotic Variables** | `r dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, n_abiotic_variables)` |
| **Geographic Coverage** | Global |
| **Temporal Coverage** | `r label_count(dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, age_min))` to `r label_count(dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, age_max))` cal yr BP |

::: {.callout-tip}
**Getting Started**: New to [VegVault]{.vegvault}? Check our [Database Access](database_access.qmd) guide for download instructions and our [Usage Examples](database_examples.qmd) for practical applications.
:::


## Spatio-temporal overview of the database content

```{r}
plan_vegetation_samples <-
  vaultkeepr::open_vault(
    path = path_to_vegvault # [config]
  ) %>%
  # Add the dataset information
  vaultkeepr::get_datasets() %>%
  # Select modern plot data and climate
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_type(
    sel_dataset_type = c(
      "vegetation_plot",
      "fossil_pollen_archive"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Add samples
  vaultkeepr::get_samples()

data_vegetation_samples <-
  vaultkeepr::extract_data(
    con = plan_vegetation_samples,
    return_raw_data = TRUE,
    verbose = FALSE
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dataset_type = stringr::str_replace_all(
      dataset_type,
      "_",
      " "
    )
  )

# The extraction leaves the connection of the plan open
DBI::dbDisconnect(purrr::chuck(plan_vegetation_samples, "db_con"))

data_vegetation_samples_space <-
  data_vegetation_samples %>%
  dplyr::distinct(dataset_type, coord_long, coord_lat)

data_vegetation_samples_time <-
  data_vegetation_samples %>%
  dplyr::distinct(dataset_id, dataset_type, age)

# Samples per 1,000 years and dataset type (ages after 1950 in the first
#   bin); the larger count of a bin is drawn first, so that both bars of a
#   bin start at zero and stay readable on the log scale
data_vegetation_samples_time_bins <-
  data_vegetation_samples_time %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_bin = (base::floor(base::pmax(age, 0) / 1e3) + 0.5) * 1e3
  ) %>%
  dplyr::count(age_bin, dataset_type, name = "n_samples") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(age_bin) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    order_draw = base::rank(-n_samples, ties.method = "first")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# The map ends at 60 degrees S, below which there is only Antarctica, unless
#   a sample lies further south
y_lim_world <-
  c(
    base::min(-60, dplyr::pull(data_vegetation_samples_space, coord_lat)),
    base::max(85, dplyr::pull(data_vegetation_samples_space, coord_lat))
  )

fig_world_empty <-
  tibble::tibble() %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  build_world_borders_layer(
    col_fill = col_beige_dark,
    col_line = NA,
    linewidth = line_size
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-90, 90, by = 30)) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-180, 180, by = 60))

fig_vegetation_space <-
  fig_world_empty +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = data_vegetation_samples_space,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = coord_long,
      y = coord_lat,
      col = dataset_type
    ),
    size = point_size / 10, # [config]
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
    values = palette_dataset_type # [config]
  ) +
  # Legend keys without the transparency of the points, in the colours of
  #   the bars
  ggplot2::guides(
    color = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(size = point_size, alpha = 1)
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    colour = "Dataset Type"
  ) +
  # One legend for both panels, in the empty ocean of the map
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.01, 0.02),
    legend.justification = c(0, 0),
    legend.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
      fill = col_beige_light, # [config]
      colour = NA
    ),
    # Room for the label 180 at the edge of the map
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 5.5, r = 20, b = 5.5, l = 5.5)
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_sf(
    xlim = c(-180, 180),
    ylim = y_lim_world,
    expand = FALSE
  )

fig_vegetation_time <-
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  # Bars drawn over each other, not stacked: stacked bars on a log scale
  #   would add the logarithms
  purrr::map(
    .x = base::sort(
      base::unique(
        dplyr::pull(data_vegetation_samples_time_bins, order_draw)
      )
    ),
    .f = ~ ggplot2::geom_col(
      data = dplyr::filter(data_vegetation_samples_time_bins, order_draw == .x),
      mapping = ggplot2::aes(
        x = age_bin,
        y = n_samples,
        fill = dataset_type
      ),
      width = 1e3
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = palette_dataset_type # [config]
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    transform = scales::transform_log1p(),
    breaks = c(1, 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5),
    labels = scales::label_comma()
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    transform = "reverse",
    breaks = seq(20e3, 0, by = -5e3),
    labels = seq(20, 0, by = -5)
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(20e3, 0)
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Age (ka cal yr BP)",
    y = "Samples per 1,000 years"
  )

path_fig_vegetation <-
  here::here(
    "Outputs/Figures/website/DB_overview/fig_db_spatiotemporal_overview.png"
  )

# The two panels are laid out on the device that writes the file (the one
#   ggsave() uses), not combined beforehand with cowplot: cowplot measures
#   the text on another device, where showtext is not switched on, so the
#   text is measured larger than it is drawn, which leaves gaps around the
#   axis titles and an oversized legend
ragg::agg_png(
  filename = path_fig_vegetation,
  width = 10,
  height = 4,
  units = "in",
  res = 300,
  background = col_beige_light # [config]
)

grid::grid.newpage()

grid::pushViewport(
  grid::viewport(
    layout = grid::grid.layout(
      nrow = 1,
      ncol = 2,
      widths = grid::unit(c(2.3, 1), "null")
    )
  )
)

print(
  fig_vegetation_space,
  vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 1)
)

print(
  fig_vegetation_time,
  vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 2)
)

invisible(grDevices::dev.off())

knitr::include_graphics(path_fig_vegetation)
```
